BDI.note: No Burundi national backbone is described.

facts.fact: Agence Ecofin reports that Tanzania earns revenue from its national ICT backbone (NICTBB), having signed separate agreements in 2023 with Malawi and Uganda to connect them to it, and resells capacity to Burundi.

Agence Ecofin reports that landlocked Burundi relies on Tanzania's cables, and that Tanzania's TTCL signed a five-year USD 3.3 million deal to resell high-speed capacity to Burundi Backbone System, after an October 2019 accord.
Agence Ecofin reports that Tanzania has three international submarine cables, 2Africa, EASSy and SEACOM.

BDI.note: The only figure is DataReportal's penetration rate, which is never used.
